**Summary**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and checked the live quote ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72), then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75 — essentially at market — which filled at $222.75 for about $9,801, comfortably inside the mandate's $10,000 per-order cap, the $20,000 daily cap (this is the only order today), and backed by $50,000 of cash in the account with no funds leaving the account. The bull case rests on the reported numbers: total net sales of $391,035 million (up 2% year over year), with Services the clear growth engine at $96,169 million (+13%) carrying a 73.9% gross margin that lifted total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income of $123,216 million; net income of $93,736 million and diluted EPS of $6.08 (Note 3 and the cash flow statement; note the statement of operations page in the filing misprints net income/EPS as $103,736 million/$8.08, which is inconsistent with the share count and the other three statements); and very strong operating cash flow of $118,254 million against only $9,447 million of capex, funding $95.0 billion of buybacks and $15.2 billion of dividends. I treated the $10.2 billion one-time State Aid tax charge and the 24.1% effective tax rate as non-recurring rather than a deterioration in earning power, and I sized the position modestly given the real offsets of an 8% decline in Greater China sales, a 7% drop in Wearables/Home/Accessories, flat iPhone revenue, and ongoing DOJ/DMA antitrust exposure. My key figures: FY2024 revenue $391,035M, operating income $123,216M, net income $93,736M, diluted EPS $6.08, operating cash flow $118,254M.
